title: The Wolf Among Us Remastered
summary: With anti-aliasing on, anything that moves leaves faded copies behind: the TAA reads 8 MSAA samples and D3DMetal gives 4. A d3d11.dll beside the game makes the shaders read the 4 there are, and one override for the game's executable loads it.
license: GPL-3.0-or-later (installer); the DLL and its source are public domain (Unlicense)

credits.name: macprotips
credits.note: Found why the trails happen, wrote the d3d11.dll that rewrites the shaders' sample reads and a test program for D3DMetal (WolfAmongUsFix 1.0). MacGameFix ships the DLL as published, with its source.

excerpts.to: ^  echo "error: could not write the override
excerpts.note: The one value in the bottle or prefix, for this executable alone: Wine loads the d3d11.dll beside the game first.

symptom: With anti-aliasing on, anything that moves leaves faded copies of itself behind.
cause: The game's TAA resolves 8x MSAA with shaders that read 8 samples a pixel. Apple GPUs have no 8x: D3DMetal says so, and still creates the game's 8x textures with 4 samples, so the reads of samples 4 to 7 return black. With black always in the mix, the history clamp never throws away dark parts of old frames.
fix: A d3d11.dll beside the game passes everything to the real d3d11.dll and, as the game creates each pixel shader, makes its reads of the missing samples use the 4 that exist. It does nothing on a device that really gives 8 samples. d3d11 = native,builtin is written for TheWolfAmongUsRemastered.exe alone, in the bottle or Steam Play prefix. Being tested: not played by MacGameFix yet.
